transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE); Marta Reyes (NebulaCart Head of Product), Jonah Klein (NebulaCart Staff ML Eng), Sana Iqbal (NebulaCart CTO)

--- Optional auto-summary present ---
Summary: quick discovery to understand NebulaCart's immediate path to a PLG/self-serve trial, TTFT needs, security constraints, and whether to start on hosted or request a Dedicated/VPC pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Monroe: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, i'm an AE, and with me are priya and daniel from the se team. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marta Reyes: doing good, thanks. we're excited — want to understand how fast we can get to a working api for our checkout assistant.
[00:11] Priya Shah: great — quick agenda: TTFT path with credits, hosting options (hosted / dedicated / private/vpc), security checklist, and next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Sana Iqbal: yep, that works. we'll mostly focus on latency and data controls — we have EU customers and some pci-adjacent workflows.
[00:25] Jonah Klein: and i want to baseline perf — 95th percentile latency targets + cost per 1k token numbers.
[00:30] Alex Monroe: perfect. to answer the TTFT question first: with our self-serve API you can be up in under an hour — create an org, api key, fire a few test requests. we also provide sandbox credits; typically for a PLG play we give 5k-15k tokens of credits depending on the starter pack.
[00:47] Jonah Klein: under an hour, that's good — but for perf are there any warmup steps? like kv cache priming or local kv?
[00:54] Priya Shah: yes, runtime uses kv cache for autoregressive workloads — for short prototypes you won't notice, for sustained token heavy loads we suggest enabling prefix caching and our batching settings. we'll share a config snippet.
[01:05] Jonah Klein: ok, great. also what models do you host? we prefer open model variants.
[01:10] Daniel Cho: we have a curated catalog — multiple open models, and some optimized variants. we also publish performance profiles per model (latency/throughput/ideal seq length). note sometimes names in the transcript are off, but we'll send the perf sheet.
[01:25] Marta Reyes: can you remind us the difference between hosted and dedicated in plain terms? our PM wants something low friction but secure.
[01:31] Alex Monroe: sure — hosted is our fastest onramp: low-friction api, quick credits, fully managed. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools just for you — predictable throughput and isolation, recommended once you need production throughput or strict data isolation. Private/VPC is when you want the control plane on our side but data plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:50] Sana Iqbal: for pci-adjacent data we likely need VPC or private — what about KMS and audit logs?
[01:56] Priya Shah: we integrate with KMS providers and support customer-managed keys for private deployments; audit logs and request-level tracing are available on Dedicated/Private tiers. hosted can be configured for EU regions and has SOC 2 compliance; for strict residency we recommend Private.
[02:12] Jonah Klein: is SOC 2 Type II available to view?
[02:15] Alex Monroe: yes we'll share a redacted attestation and a security brief — link to security packet: https://redwood.example/scc/soc2 (note: placeholder).
[02:25] Marta Reyes: perfect. what about latency targets — we were hoping for sub-250ms 95p for short prompts (<=256 tokens) on production. realistic?
[02:34] Priya Shah: for short sequences on Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching tuned for low latency, sub-250ms 95p is achievable on certain model sizes. hosted latency varies by model and region; our catalog includes 95p numbers measured in our infra. we should run a bench with your prompt set to be definitive.
[02:51] Jonah Klein: ok the bench is key. can you run a run for both hosted and dedicated so we can compare cost curves?
[02:59] Daniel Cho: absolutely — we'll supply a benchmark plan (requests per second, seq lengths, concurrency) and run across model variants and quantization settings. we'll show cost-per-1k-token and 95p latency.
[03:12] Alex Monroe: on credits — for this trial we'd propose 10k free credits to get through prompt tuning and basic integration. that usually covers a decent number of iterations.
[03:20] Marta Reyes: 10k sounds reasonable. do credits apply to dedicated or only hosted?
[03:24] Alex Monroe: credits are typically applied to hosted sandbox orgs. for Dedicated we can do a reserved pilot or a short-term burst allotment to simulate production.
[03:32] Sana Iqbal: timeline wise, we want to present to execs in two weeks. so we need a bench and first-call demo by next week ideally.
[03:40] Priya Shah: we can run a bench next week, yes. if Jonah shares the prompt set by thursday we can schedule the demo and have numbers for your exec slot.
[03:50] Jonah Klein: i'll bundle representative queries and traffic profile — i'll anonymize any PHI/pci bits.
[03:54] Marta Reyes: what telemetry is visible in the console out-of-the-box?
[03:59] Daniel Cho: console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and traces. you can also stream logs to your SIEM. retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has standard retention windows but we can discuss extended retention as an add-on.
[04:15] Jonah Klein: and for billing how granular is it? we want per-environment cost separation.
[04:19] Alex Monroe: billing supports orgs and subprojects with tags. you can separate dev/prod and set quotas. we'll include a billing example in the docs we send.
[04:27] Sana Iqbal: any gotchas on model parity when moving from hosted to dedicated?
[04:31] Priya Shah: sometimes we switch to a quantized variant to hit cost targets — we maintain functionally equivalent models but there can be tiny quality diffs. Redwood Optimize helps recommend quantization and batching profiles per workload to minimize quality regression. we run evals on your prompts to quantify the regressions.
[04:48] Marta Reyes: good — we'll want the evals. in terms of procurement, what's the minimal commercial commitment if we want Dedicated?
[04:55] Alex Monroe: typical Dedicated pilots are monthly reserved capacity agreements (smallest block depends on model and region). we can discuss a limited pilot that mirrors your expected sustained RPS. I'll include sample numbers.
[05:05] Jonah Klein: any competitor quirks we should test for? like better latency on Mistral Cloud for certain ops?
[05:11] Daniel Cho: we see different providers/severs excel at different model families; we'll make sure the bench includes baseline runs so you can compare.
[05:18] Marta Reyes: ok next steps — credits, bench, send security docs, and a follow-up demo.
[05:23] Alex Monroe: yep. recap action items: we'll grant 10k credits to your sandbox, Priya will schedule a bench/demo, I'll send the security packet and starter pricing. Jonah to share prompt set and traffic profile.
[05:34] Jonah Klein: i'll get that to you by thursday; one more quick question — what support SLAs are available during the trial?
[05:40] Alex Monroe: trial orgs get email support and a fast-track touch from AE/SE. Dedicated gets SLA-backed uptime options that we can walk through as you approach production.
[05:50] Sana Iqbal: fine — please include the rollback/fallback behavior in the docs — we want automatic fallback to cheaper model variants if a node is unhealthy.
[05:57] Priya Shah: yep we've got smart routing and automatic fallback policies, including canary and A/B rollouts — will include examples.
[06:06] Marta Reyes: thanks everyone, this was super helpful. let's reconvene after the bench runs.
[06:10] Alex Monroe: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links and invites.

--- End transcript ---
